title: Postoperative auditory outcomes in total temporomandibular joint replacement: fossa–canal proximity and tinnitus risk
html: Total temporomandibular joint replacement (TMJR) is an established treatment for advanced ankylosis; however, postoperative auditory complications, such as tinnitus, remain poorly characterized. This post-hoc observational analysis evaluated whether postoperative prosthetic fossa–external auditory meatus (EAM) distance is associated with postoperative tinnitus after TMJR for ankylosis, and explored preoperative ankylosis–EAM proximity and tinnitus resolution. Patients aged 18–40 years undergoing TMJR with orthognathic surgery with ≥12 months follow-up and postoperative cone-beam computed tomography were evaluated.
